transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Pegasus CTO), Sofia (Pegasus Security Lead), Liam (Procurement)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Walkthrough of Pegasus vendor security form and SIG / CAIQ mapping. Main asks: SOC 2 and ISO evidence, KMS/customer-managed keys, retention of audit logs, SSO integration details, and data residency assurances for EU customers.

[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everybody, thanks for joining, um appreciate you making time right before the holiday week. quick intros, i'll kick it off. i'm jordan, ae on the redwood inference team. priya is our solutions engineer who will drive the technical bits.
[00:18] Mark (CTO): thanks, jordan. yep i'm mark, cto. sofia is on for security. liam in procurement. hope this will be pretty brisk.
[00:28] Priya (SE): hey all, hi. quick agenda: we'll run through the sig/caiq, call out where we can drop direct evidence links, and discuss kms/key custody and sso. then q&a and action items. sound good?
[00:39] Sofia (Security Lead): yes thanks. our vendor form is fairly detailed, and we also have an internal addendum about EU data residency for checkout flows.
[00:47] Jordan: perfect. okay i'll share my screen — i'm going to pull up the high-level CAIQ mapping so we can cross-reference your questions. note the auto-export sometimes scribbles the answer fields so i'll read the statements too.

[01:10] Priya: starting with compliance posture — we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, both audited, and we can share redacted reports for vendor review. the SOC 2 covers common criteria: access controls, change management, logging. for iso we can provide scope doc and cert.
[01:28] Sofia: great. can you confirm retention period for audit logs and where they live? we need 12 months plus e-discovery for certain EU regs.
[01:36] Priya: yes, audit logs are retained by default 13 months in hosted, and in Dedicated/Private you can configure longer retention. logs are stored in our telemetry cluster (note: auto transcribed as "telemetry clus ter"), and are encrypted at rest. we can provide an examples log export (redacted) as evidence.
[01:55] Mark: who holds the keys? specifically, do you do customer-managed KMS or is it vendor-managed? and do you support HSM-backed customer keys?
[02:04] Jordan: good question. short answer: we have multiple options. hosted customers can choose Redwood-managed keys in our cloud KMS, or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer-managed cloud KMS. for private/on-prem deployments we support HSM integrations — we've partnered with hardware providers for HSM attestation.
[02:22] Priya: to add — on AWS we support AWS KMS CMKs and can configure key policies with customer principals. for GCP we use CMEK patterns. we also have an HSM-backed option for Dedicated if the contract requires it. i'll note that some auto transcript things call it "h-m-s" or "ash-ems" — sorry for the noise.

[02:48] Sofia: do you have any customers doing full BYOK where they rotate keys independently? we need to see rotation policies and proof of separation of duty.
[02:55] Priya: yes, several customers do independent key rotation. rotation intervals and split knowledge are enforced via KMS policies and RBAC. we can provide a diagram of key custody flows and a redacted rotation log.

[03:12] Liam (Procurement): on the CAIQ, there are a few questions around cryptographic algorithms — AES, RSA, etc. can you state algorithms and cert levels?
[03:20] Priya: encryption at rest uses AES-256, TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, and keys are wrapped with customer CMKs if BYOK. for attestation we can reference our vendor crypto policy and the HSM FIPS 140-2/3 compliance notes where applicable.

[03:38] Mark: residency — our payment data must remain in EU regions. how does redwood ensure region scoping for inference requests and model hosting?
[03:46] Jordan: we have routing policies that pin requests to regions; for hosted we offer EU region endpoints and a private control plane option to restrict model weights and inference to EU datacenters. for strictest customers we recommend Private deployment or a Dedicated reserved pool located in the EU.
[04:02] Priya: important: when using hosted with EU routing, we still recommend contract-level residency clauses and a data processing addendum (DPA) to declare guarantees. we'll share our DPA template.

[04:20] Sofia: audit question — do you offer immutable audit logs or tamper-evident traces? we need evidence for chain of custody.
[04:26] Priya: yes, logs are write-once in our audit store with integrity checks; we can provide an export showing the hash chain example. some of the language in your form may say "write once / tamper proof" which we map to our WORM-like storage and checksum metadata.

[04:46] Jordan: switching to identity — SSO and RBAC. we support SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning. role model supports admin/write/view separation: tenant admin, app admin, and read-only ops.
[04:59] Mark: does SCIM map to groups and role binding? we want automated provisioning of service accounts.
[05:05] Priya: yes, SCIM can provision groups that map to RBAC roles. service accounts can be scoped and bound to API routes; we have token policies and rotation TTLs.

[05:20] Sofia: can you demonstrate the audit trail for who changed role bindings? we need change history for SSO-provisioned accounts.
[05:26] Priya: every RBAC change is logged with actor, timestamp, and before/after state. those events are included in the audit exports. we'll attach a sample (sanitized).

[05:40] Liam: procurement note — we'll need redwood's insurance cert and subcontractor list as part of the legal packet.
[05:46] Jordan: yes we'll put that in the security pack. we'll also include our SOC 2, iso certificate, pen test summary, and the CAIQ export with populated answers.

[06:00] Mark: about SIG mapping — can you walk through a few tricky control items? e.g., network segmentation and tenant isolation for multi-tenant hosted env.
[06:10] Priya: absolutely. multi-tenant isolation is provided by runtime sandboxing, namespace isolation and network policies. for higher assurance we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) where customers get isolated GPU pools and network boundaries. in Private deployments you get full network control. the CAIQ answers indicate which controls are applicable to each deployment mode.
[06:34] Sofia: on the CAIQ question about third-party code scans and supply chain — do you run SBOMs for model artifacts?
[06:41] Priya: we produce SBOM-like manifests for models we ship and for dependencies in our control plane. for customer-supplied models we recommend customers run their own scans, but we can offer a review service as part of an enterprise engagement.

[06:58] Jordan: quick side note: some of the auto transcript replacements might show our product names weirdly — e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> "red wood dedicated" — apologies if that shows up.

[07:06] Mark: ok thanks. on evidence delivery — what's the preferred format? spreadsheet? pdf? links?
[07:11] Jordan: CAIQ we export a spreadsheet (.xlsx) with references to artifacts; SOC and ISO are PDFs. For logs and sample exports we'll provide redacted CSVs or cloud storage links with limited TTL. evidence links are preferred for speed, but we can package a zip for procurement if needed.

[07:28] Sofia: about redaction — we require customer-identifying fields removed. can you do that?
[07:32] Priya: yes, we redact PII and customer identifiers in artifacts. SOC 2 reports are redacted for customer names and internal IPs by default.

[07:43] Liam: contractually, do you accept an addendum for EU data residency and a clause for KMS BYOK?
[07:50] Jordan: we do. our legal team will review the addendum; BYOK clauses are common and we sign key custody annexes. we'll flag a few items where Private deployment is recommended for air-gap needs.

[08:02] Mark: any blockers for us to start a pilot with EU routing and CMK?
[08:07] Priya: no blockers technically. two things: you need a contract with residency guarantee and we need to set up key access with your KMS principals (we'll provide an IAM policy template). also we'll want to run a short performance benchmark to ensure latency within your SLOs — we can include that in the pilot scope.

[08:27] Sofia: ok good. can you share the IAM policy template now?
[08:30] Jordan: yes i'll put it in the pack.

[08:34] Priya: moving on — penetration testing and vuln disclosures. we do annual pen tests and vuln scanning; for enterprise customers we can discuss shared pen test windows or an attestation letter.

[08:48] Mark: do you allow customer audits on premise? sometimes legal asks for that.
[08:52] Jordan: for hosted, we don't do on-site audits but we provide third-party reports and allow for audit rights via contract clauses. for Private we can negotiate on-site or remote audits depending on the scope.

[09:04] Sofia: there are some SIG items around business continuity and disaster recovery RTO/RPO for model serving — what's your standard?
[09:11] Priya: typical RTOs depend on deployment: hosted has multi-region failover with RTO in minutes for control plane features; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed RTOs per contract. we'll share our DR runbook summary and RTO/RPO targets.

[09:29] Jordan: okay we're about to open for questions — please call out any line items in your form you want to review live.

[09:36] Mark: item 27 asks about encryption key destruction and end-of-contract key handling — what happens when customer ends contract?
[09:44] Priya: upon contract termination we support key escrow transfer procedures. with BYOK, you retain ownership and we delete wrapped keys after verification. we provide certificate of destruction and an export of final logs. We'll follow a verified wipe procedure for any customer data held in the vendor environment.

[10:02] Sofia: can you detail the timeline for evidence delivery? we have a procurement gating milestone Jan 18th.
[10:09] Jordan: timeline wise: we'll send the CAIQ export and SOC/ISO by 2027-01-04; Priya will prepare KMS diagrams and sample logs by 2027-01-06; you send back any follow-up questions and the completed customer form by 2027-01-10. that should leave enough time for procurement to review by Jan 18.

[10:30] Liam: procurement question — any discounts tied to Dedicated vs Hosted? not security but matters for budget planning.
[10:34] Jordan: pricing is separate; we can provide a preliminary cost comparison. Dedicated has a reserved capacity commitment, so discounts apply at commit tiers. we'll put a pricing note in the follow-up but legal/security evidence is the immediate path.

[10:48] Priya: another small note about model weights — for Private deployments customers can keep model artifacts on-prem. for hosted, model artifacts are stored in regional S3 buckets with encryption; we can pin model versions and restrict access.

[11:05] Mark: on the CAIQ control that asks for "logs accessible to customer" — do you offer a console or API to pull logs?
[11:10] Priya: yes, customers can pull logs via API or through the Redwood Console with role-based access. for higher assurance we can set up a read-only log shipping to customer-owned S3 for ingestion into their SIEM.

[11:26] Sofia: are there SIEM connectors documented? we use Splunk and Sumo.
[11:30] Priya: we have docs for Splunk HEC and S3-based ingestion; we'll include links.

[11:38] Jordan: okay any final questions?
[11:40] Mark: one last on subcontractors — do you use third-party hosting or managed services? need list and controls.
[11:46] Priya: yes we use cloud providers for compute and storage; subcontractor list and SOC attestations for those providers are included in our security pack. we'll also map CAIQ responses to show where cloud provider controls are leveraged.

[11:58] Sofia: great. thanks everyone. we'll look for the pack and then we'll score items that need a walkthrough.
[12:03] Jordan: perfect. quick recap of action items and dates — i'll read them out.
[12:08] Jordan: ACTIONS: Jordan to send CAIQ + SOC/ISO evidence by Jan 4. Priya to send KMS diagrams and sample redacted logs by Jan 6. Sofia to send completed residency matrix by Jan 10. schedule deep dive in second week of Jan for Private/KMS if needed.
[12:24] Liam: thanks all. we'll follow up in email. happy holidays.
[12:28] Mark: thanks. end call.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some words auto-transcribed (HSM, KV cache, Redwood Dedicated) may be slightly garbled. speaker attribution largely correct but may have small errors.
